items.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: And they were great players working for — ... You know at one point Billy Butterfield was getting his 802 card, so was Conrad Gozzo and I.

ctx.x: With Red it was like a low figure and you were lucky to get it. And not that he — it was a financial problem that he could not cope with. That was an old trick, and I should not take too much time on it, but if you worked a week here and then had two days off, they’d change the payday to conform to the next — Now after, with Claude, he had more backing and everything and that was not it. But the salary pre-war I would say ran like $150, something like that a week. Like we had Irving Fazola and Nick Fatool and…

Right. Thank you. And they were great players working for — You know at one point Billy Butterfield was getting his 802 card, so was Conrad Gozzo and I. And Billy came in and played third trumpet while he was getting his 802 card. And in doing an interview on WKCR they looked at the personnel on different record dates, and he said, “Are you sure that was the trumpet section?” It was.
